title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of light-signalling devices (lamps) for power-driven vehicles and their trailers (LSD), version 1.6.0
scope_summary: UN R148 type-approves light-signalling lamps: position, end-outline marker, parking, daytime running, stop, direction indicator, side marker, reversing, rear fog, manoeuvring and rear-registration plate lamps, plus reversing projectors. It covers lamps for motor vehicles and their trailers, including category L variants, intended for installation under UN R48 (M/N/O), R53 and R74 (L) and R86 (agricultural tractors).
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the following light-signalling devices (lamps): Rear-registration plate illuminating lamps Direction indicator lamps Position lamps Stop lamps End-outline marker lamps Reversing lamps Manoeuvring lamps Rear fog lamps Parking lamps Daytime running lamps Side marker lamps Reversing projectors.
vehicle_categories: T (agricultural/forestry tractors, via installation Regulation No. 86)
applies_to_components: Stop lamps (including central high-mounted stop lamps)
Front and rear end-outline marker lamps
Replaceable light source modules used in these lamps
Electronic light source control gear / variable intensity control being part of the lamp
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp units
Assemblies of two independent lamps (D) and interdependent lamp systems (Y)
relation_to_other_regulations: Combines the provisions of UN Regulations Nos. 4, 6, 7, 23, 38, 50, 77, 87 and 91 into a single Regulation (simplification of lighting regulations, IWG SLR).
The definitions of the latest series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48 apply unless otherwise specified here or in installation Regulations Nos. 53, 74 and 86.

Sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of installation Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 apply where verification at lamp approval is feasible; the 01 series is accompanied by amendments to R48, R53, R74 and R86.
Replaceable light sources must be approved to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128; LED substitute light sources per R128; standard light sources per R.E.5.
Tell-tale signals refer to paragraphs of R48 (e.g. 6.5.8, 6.19.8) and R53 (6.3.8).
Lamps grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated with lamps approved under other Regulations may carry a single approval mark.
Non-replaceable filament light sources: IEC 60809 Ed. 4 para 4.11; lamp holders: IEC 60061.
EMC: lamps shall not cause malfunction of other systems; compliance with EMC requirements is relevant to the vehicle type (i.e. UN R10 at vehicle level).
Conformity of production per 1958 Agreement Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).

defined_terms.definition: Lamps differing in essential respects such as trade name/mark, optical system characteristics, light source category or module identification code, lamp category, variable intensity control, or sequential activation; colour change of light source/filter or use of LED substitute light sources does not constitute a change of type.
Physically included in the lamp body or external, separated or not, and declared by the applicant as part of the lamp system.
Direction indicators activatable in different modes (sequential or not) without modification of optical characteristics do not constitute different types.

Two independent lamps of the same function approved as lamps marked 'D', deemed a single lamp, meeting maximum intensity with all lit and minimum intensity if either fails; applicable to position, end-outline marker, stop, daytime running and direction indicator lamps.

A system of interdependent lamps approved as lamps marked 'Y' that meets the requirements when all its lamps operate together, applicable to position, end-outline marker, stop, daytime running and direction indicator lamps.

defined_terms.term: Light source module specific identification code
defined_terms.definition: Code starting with 'MD' followed by the approval mark without the circle, marked on replaceable light source modules and on the lamp.

applicability_hints: Any rear-registration plate lamp, indicator, position/stop/tail, DRL, side marker, reversing, rear fog, parking, manoeuvring lamp or reversing projector (ground projection behind vehicle) falls under R148, regardless of light source technology (filament, LED module, non-replaceable LED).
Headlamps, front fog lamps and cornering lamps are not in the R148 scope list (covered by separate road illumination regulation); retro-reflectors are not covered either.
Position lamps approved under R148 are automatically deemed approved as end-outline marker lamps.
A separate approval (symbol) is needed for each function; multifunction rear combination lamps get one approval per function but may carry a single approval mark.
Lamps mounted inside the vehicle behind a rear window (e.g. interior CHMSL) are approved with sample plates replicating the rear window optics.
Electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control outside the lamp body but declared part of the lamp must be marked with ID and manufacturer name.
Replaceable light source modules must carry 'MD' identification codes and be tool-removable, tamperproof and non-interchangeable.
Lamps incorporating a vehicle manufacturer logo (max 100 cm2) are allowed, except stop lamps, direction indicators and reversing lamps.
Front position lamps incorporating infrared generators (e.g. for night vision/driver monitoring sensors) must meet photometry with and without IR operation.
Lamps intended for category L vehicles (MA, MR, MS, 11x, 12, LM1) and agricultural tractors (via R86) are also approved under R148.
Sequential direction indicators and variable-intensity lamps (R2, RM2, S2, S4, 2b, F2) are covered, including the intensity control system.
Replacement lamps restricted to vehicles in use (due to light source restrictions) are approved with a note in the communication form.
Lamps using LED substitute light sources (R128) need repeated photometry/colorimetry but no new type.
Lamps relying on vehicle tell-tale for failure detection are restricted to vehicles fitted with such tell-tale.
Lamps must not cause EMC disturbances, but EMC compliance is assessed at vehicle level.
